audit.whatIsWrong: The whole page tracks the wrong ability. Every reference calls Twofold Hex her 'blink' / 'escape' — in several places literally 'Twofold Hex (Blink)'. It also repeatedly credits her with a root.
audit.why: Riot's text: Twofold Hex (Q) is a missile that curses enemies, recast to draw the curses back through them — no blink, no root. The escape is Across the Veil (W), 22/21/20/19/18s: she leaps, lands in the spirit realm, becomes invisible and gains Move Speed. Nothing in her kit roots; her R and E slow. Tracking her Q cooldown while her W is the escape is advice that gets the reader killed.
audit.corrected: Across the Veil, with its 22s rank-1 cooldown, now occupies the tracked-cooldown slot across focus, tldr, winCon, enemyWin, loading, ahead, the breakdown block, the dos/donts and reports 1/3/5/9/10/12/13, plus the spikes, whys and phase prose. Every root claim replaced with the slow that actually exists. wants.foe[0] now describes what Twofold Hex really does.

audit.whatIsWrong: The stored chart gave Renekton levels 3, 4-5, first item and 2+ items and gave Aurora level 1 — inverted at six of seven rows against the packet.
audit.why: packet.levelChart = [Renekton, Aurora, Aurora, Aurora, Aurora, Aurora, Aurora]. The mirror audit already rebuilt Aurora's side to exactly that chart, so leaving this side as-is would have the two pages contradict each other on six rows. whys[2], whys[3] and whys[6] on this page already argue Aurora wins those stages.
audit.corrected: Six rows flipped as one atomic group, win[N] paired with phases[N].side, ratings adjusted, and phases[1].why / phases[2].why / phases[3].why / phases[5].why / phases[6].why plus whys[0] and whys[1] rewritten so the reasoning matches the new owner.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-2 spike was sold as Renekton's 'only clean window' with no cooldown attached, and level 1 was given to Aurora.
audit.why: Across the Veil is not available until level 2 at the earliest, and it is 22s at rank 1 — the longest basic cooldown in her kit. Level 1 is the one stage where she has no leap and Renekton's Fury autos are simply better at melee range.
audit.corrected: whys[0] now states the level-1 melee advantage; the level-2 rows now state that Across the Veil is what takes the window away; the 22s figure is written into dosFull[0].d, dontsFull[1].d and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemisation named no anti-heal despite Aurora healing off every spell she lands.
audit.why: missingInteractions flags 'needs-antiheal': Spirit Abjuration (P) exorcises spirits from damaged enemies that follow her and heal her, so a poke-heavy Aurora sustains through chip damage.
audit.corrected: report[8].t now calls Executioner's Calling and names Spirit Abjuration as the reason.

edits.before: At level 1 she wins every trade — her Q poke out-ranges your autos and you have no dash to close yet, so just last-hit safely and do not waste HP proving who is tougher. The lane turns the moment you hit level 2: E in, immediately use your empowered-W to stun her in place before she can react with Twofold Hex, then Q heal through any return damage and dice back out. That single window is the entire early game — if she burns Twofold Hex to blink away from something else first, you get a free all-in; if she has it, you have to fake the E and bait it before committing.
edits.after: At level 1 she has no leap yet, so melee range is genuinely yours — take the auto trades with Fury when she steps up to last-hit, but never walk out to her Q. The lane turns against you at level 2: Across the Veil comes online, and now your only clean sequence is E in, empowered-W stun before she can leap, Q heal through the return damage, dice back out. If she burns Across the Veil on something else first, you get a free all-in; if she has it, fake the E and bait the leap before committing.

edits.before: Levels 4 through 6 belong to Aurora because her blink is up more often and her Q poke forces trades on her terms rather than yours. Track the Twofold Hex cooldown obsessively — your only winning trade is the one where you E in while it is down and land the empowered-W stun before she can use it. At level 6 your Dominus gives you the HP buffer to survive her full burst combo, but her ultimate lets her escape any extended fight cleanly; do not chase through her ult displacement or you feed a free wave of damage. The realistic goal is a small CS and health lead, not a solo kill.
edits.after: Levels 4 through 6 belong to Aurora because her leap is up more often and her Q poke forces trades on her terms rather than yours. Track Across the Veil obsessively — 22s at rank 1, and your only winning trade is the one where you E in while it is down and land the empowered-W stun. At level 6 your Dominus gives you the HP buffer to survive her burst, but her ultimate leaves a slowing zone she can teleport across; do not chase through it or you eat a free wave of damage. The realistic goal is a small CS and health lead, not a solo kill.

edits.before: Once Aurora has two AP items she wins the extended 1v1 — repeated Twofold Hex blinks, her root interrupting your follow-up E, and burst damage that outpaces your Q healing mean the solo duel is over. Stop trying to run the kill pattern and shift to split-pushing pressure: you clear faster, force a response, and her team cannot send her alone to answer you. If she matches, trade wave-for-wave and play for the roam rather than the 1v1.

notes: This entry tracked the wrong ability end to end: Twofold Hex (Q, a curse missile with a recast) was labelled her blink and her escape, and she was repeatedly credited with a root she does not have. The escape is Across the Veil (W, 22s at rank 1, leap into invisibility). Every occurrence is corrected. The level chart was inverted at six of seven rows against the packet and against the already-audited mirror; flipped as one atomic group. diff/diffRating left at TRICKY 7.5/10 — the mirror audit noted the rating scale is not applied consistently across this champion's file and there is no safe basis for a new number; that is a champion-level question, recorded below.
